•  Talk about hopes with hope to

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "Where I'm going." Say: "Tonight we talk about our plans, our hopes, and our goals."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "I'm going to take a computer class." • "I hope to get my diploma." • "Then → Now → Next."
Goals are personal (important): every goal is a good goal. "Learn more English" and "help my kids" are great goals. Learners don't have to share personal details; an invented goal is fine. Don't ask about immigration status, money, or family problems.
Lesson plan: Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Teacher notes.

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these five things.
Every goal is a good goal.
I can talk about a plan with going to.
I can talk about hopes with hope to.
I can say what I will do first.
I can choose going to, will, or hope to.
I can give a 1–2 minute talk about my goals.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: I'm going to take a computer class. Goal 2: I hope to get my diploma. / I hope I'll… Goal 3: First, I'll ask about classes.
Goal 4: going to (planned), will (decided now, a promise), or hope to (not sure). Goal 5: Then → Now → Next. Learners also read a community college flyer and write a graduation talk (6–8 sentences) in Read & Write.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.

Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson thirteen. Listening. Sofia was a Level 3 student. Tonight, she's talking to the class about her goals. Listen.
Mr. Novak: Welcome back, Sofia! Please tell us about your goals.
Sofia: Thank you. Three years ago, I came to this class. I was nervous, and my English was not very good.
Sofia: Now I work at a hotel, and I can talk with my coworkers in English.
Mr. Novak: That's great. What's your main goal?
Sofia: My main goal is to get a medical assistant certificate. I hope to work at a clinic.
Mr. Novak: How are you going to do that?
Sofia: First, I'm going to take a computer class at the community college. It starts in January.
Sofia: After that, I'll apply for the certificate program. And I hope to help my kids with their homework, too.
Mr. Novak: Any advice for the class?
Sofia: Yes. Come every week, and don't be afraid to make mistakes. You can do it!
Mr. Novak: Thank you, Sofia. Good luck!
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

slides.notes:
Box 4 (2 min): which one? Read the table. Then plan to / want to / hope to + verb. Each click shows one row.
Three forms, three meanings: going to = already planned. will = decided now or a promise. hope to = you want it, but you're not sure.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Goal Ladder + Talk Rehearsal · 12 min.
Model your own talk first (1 min): give your 1-minute talk (Then → Now → Next, one reason). Example: "Ten years ago, I was a cook. Now I'm a volunteer teacher. Next year, I'm going to take a Spanish class, because I want to understand my neighbors. I hope to visit Mexico." Point to each part on the board as you speak.
Goal Ladder, pairs (4 min): each learner fills in the ladder on the Talk Time page for one goal (step 1: I'll…; step 2: I'm going to…; top: I hope to…). A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. It's a plan.   b. It's a hope.

a. She planned it last week.   b. She decided now.
a. It's a fixed plan.   b. It's a hope.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "I'm going to take a class in March." (a) • 2 "I hope to open my own business." (b) • 3 "OK, I'll call them tomorrow." (b) • 4 "I'm meeting the counselor on Monday." (a)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 to get, 2 going to, 3 I'll, 4 to. C: answers will vary (for example I'm going to save money for a car. / I hope to get a promotion.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the future forms (A) and with the forms (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them in Week 15 before the final). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 15 at 6:00, before the final exam.
